problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z<1.63).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.7\,$ | $\,0.0436\,$ | $\,0.0427\,$ | $\,0.0419\,$ |
| $\,-1.6\,$ | $\,0.0537\,$ | $\,0.0526\,$ | $\,0.0516\,$ |
| $\,-1.5\,$ | $\,0.0655\,$ | $\,0.0643\,$ | $\,0.0630\,$ |

$P(Z<1.63)=$
{{field-1}}

activity_context.topic_title: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution

feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/1b3a9a3891150ae0b187c79e2305d391f719898a9efe42b42e7bf0777d965aa3.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<1.65).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/fd2f95626ff0a8f1aa59e94e18fddaae63216ee5962f4b7264ea952db76619b6.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>-1.65).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/94dfdaf777193a2a4b39e7e13c1297c3497c3d4dd474599a16a1bd4f559602b0.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<1.65) & =P(Z>-1.65) \\  & =1-P(Z<-1.65) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.65) \\  & =1-0.0495 \\  & =0.9505.\end{aligned}
$$
